scope: Independent recomputation over the preserved W1 exact-C3 source workset. No parser profiling, native test, full original gate or RSS measurement is performed by this review.
resource_interpretation: The only baseline inputs whose cache eligibility changes are these two Rust files. The largest current Python input is 64669 characters, so this literal does not add a larger Python baseline input to retention.

The two additional Rust input strings plus same-length masked outputs represent 1466228 retained characters before Python object/LRU overhead; actual representation bytes and overall RSS were not measured.

100 Rust and 71 Python baseline unique texts fit their separate 128-entry caches. Mutation tests introduce additional full-text versions, so this does not prove a bound on the runtime working set or guarantee freedom from eviction.

There are 81 declared rust_code calls across the two previously oversize files in one complete validate. This is structural workload evidence, not an observed hit count, elapsed-time attribution or predicted 300-second pass.

The prior theoretical full-cache capacity discussion remains a capacity warning, not a description of this measured baseline corpus. Original process/resource controls and the 300-second timeout remain the acceptance test.
decision: The actual coverage supports the narrowly targeted 512-Ki-character retention change; retain the original complete source/test/resource gates and preserve C3 timeout evidence.
